key_insight: A cross-cohort serum proteomics study identified 19 circulating proteins associated with ALS survival, with GSN and IGFBP2 showing added prognostic value.
clinical_relevance: These blood-based markers could improve patient risk stratification and support more precise prognosis in ALS beyond standard clinical factors and NfL.
method: Analyzed serum from 741 ALS patients across independent Israel and UK cohorts.
Used two orthogonal proteomics platforms: mass spectrometry and Olink PEA.
Cross-validated protein-survival associations across cohorts and platforms.
evidence_signal: The findings were evaluated in a large survival study and replicated across two independent cohorts using complementary proteomic technologies.
watch_item: These are prognostic biomarker candidates, so further external validation and assay standardization are needed before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Circulating protein profiling identifies prognostic biomarkers in amyotrophic lateral Sclerosis
